description: Figure 4 is a bar chart illustrating the number of participants (N = 6) who identified each evaluation criterion as beneficial in the user study. The horizontal axis lists the evaluation criteria: “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs),” “Concise summaries and explanations,” and “Clarity of the interface.” The vertical axis represents the count of participants, ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Each criterion is represented by a single vertical bar, colored in a uniform shade of gray. The bar for “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)” reaches a height of 6, indicating all participants found this beneficial. The bar for “Concise summaries and explanations” reaches a height of 5, and the bar for “Clarity of the interface” reaches a height of 4. The bars are arranged in descending order of participant count from left to right, visually emphasizing the most valued features. No legend or additional annotations are present, and the chart is presented with a minimalist design, focusing solely on the comparative counts across the three criteria.
